items.text: A truck carrying 100 beehives in China was involved in an accident, and the beehives were thrown open and scattered across the lanes. People sealed off the motorway to protect other drivers while keepers tried to coax the bees back into the hives. Many of the bees returned, but some of the hives were left in the road in hope that the swarms would return overnight. Difficult words: scatter (to break into many pieces over an area), coax (to make somebody to do something), swarm (a group of insects). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A truck is carrying millions of bees in their beehives and the truck gets into an accident on a motorway in China. The beehives scatter across the motorway and the bees fly out. While the beekeepers get some of the bees to go back to the truck, the police close the motorway to keep other drivers safe. The keepers leave some of the hives in the road because they hope that the bees will return to the hives during the night. Difficult words: beehive (a home for bees that the bees make), scatter (to break up), beekeeper (a person who takes care of bees). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A truck is on a motorway in China. The truck has millions of bees on it. It also has beehives on it. The truck has an accident. The bees fly everywhere. The police close the motorway. They want to keep the bees away from people. The beehives are all over the motorway. The beekeepers try to catch the bees. They catch some of them. Some beehives are still in the road. The keepers leave them there. They think that the bees will come back. Difficult words: motorway (a big and busy road), beehive (a home for bees), beekeeper (a person who works with bees). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Police in Spain seized one of the largest discoveries of taxidermy animals in Europe. Police found a giant warehouse near Valencia that contained nearly 200 ivory elephant tusks and a collection of more than 1,000 stuffed animals, including rhinos, polar bears, elephants, lions, leopards, and a lynx. The estimated worth of the haul was 32 million dollars, and it included over 400 protected species. Some of them were extinct, such as the scimitar oryx, that was declared extinct by the International Union for Conservation of Nature in 2000. Some animals were severely threatened, such as the Bengal tiger and addax, a white antelope. The owner of the warehouse hasn’t been arrested; however, he’s under investigation for smuggling and for crimes against flora and fauna. Officials said they would investigate whether any documentation justified the possession of the animals. Difficult words: taxidermy (cleaning, preserving and filling the skins of dead animals to make them look as if they’re alive), haul (something that’s been stolen or that’s possessed illegally), extinct (a species that no longer exists). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Spanish police found a large building near the city of Valencia, which was full of taxidermy animals. 1,000 animals are there, for example, rhinos, polar bears and lions. More than 400 animals were protected or extinct . Among the protected animals were Bengal tigers and a white antelope called addax. One of the extinct animals was the scimitar oryx, which became extinct in the year 2000. There were also nearly 200 elephant tusks. Police didn’t arrest the owner of the warehouse, but they said that they had to find out if the man kept the animals legally. They investigated the man for smuggling both animals and plants. Difficult words: extinct (an animal or plant which no longer exists), smuggle (to move something illegally in or out of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Spanish police find a large building near the city of Valencia. The building is full of stuffed animals. 200 elephant tusks are there . 1,000 animals are there. They are animals like rhinos, elephants, and polar bears. More than 400 animals are protected or extinct. A protected animal is an animal which people must keep safe. An extinct animal is an animal which doesn’t exist in the world anymore. Police don’t arrest the owner of the animals. They ask him many questions. They need to know if the man owns the animals legally. It is possible that he smuggles the animals to Spain. Difficult words: stuffed (a dead animal which has the skin filled with special material, and the animal looks alive), tusk (a long tooth of an elephant), smuggle (to move something illegally in or out of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In New Zealand, inflation and price increases have sent food prices sky-high, and large numbers of people are foraging to get food. Foraging is popular in Christchurch, the largest city in the South Island, where earthquakes demolished over 7,500 homes in 2010 and 2011. Local authorities designated a ‘ red zone ’ that was considered too unstable to rebuild buildings. Many backyard fruit trees were left to grow wild and continue to grow fruit, and they made it a heaven for food foragers . In the beginning, many people came out of necessity, as they realized that they could pick and eat fruit, walnuts, or mushrooms for free. However, they quickly saw that foraging was a great way to connect with nature, learn about seasons, and learn what grows in the seasons. Difficult words: foraging (going from place to place and searching for things that you can eat or use), red zone (an area that’s dangerous or forbidden), forager (a person or animal that goes from place to place to search for things that they can eat or use). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2010 and 2011, two big earthquakes destroyed more than 7,500 homes in Christchurch, the largest city in New Zealand’s South Island. A part of the city became too dangerous to build new houses there. Empty streets and backyard gardens stayed, and fruit trees continued to grow fruit. Inflation and prices increased very much in recent years, and people looked for ways to get cheap food. They turned to foraging, or going from place to place to find things which they could eat, and they discovered the wild gardens in Christchurch. Many people started to enjoy this activity, since they could spend more time in nature, and they learned about what grew at what time of year. They said that wild fruit tasted better than the fruit from supermarkets. Difficult words: backyard (the area behind a house), inflation (when prices are growing, and the power of money is smaller), turn to (to start doing something new). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Christchurch is a large city in New Zealand’s South Island. Two big earthquakes hurt the city in 2010 and 2011. The earthquakes destroy more than 7,500 homes. A part of the city becomes too dangerous . It is not possible to build new houses there. Gardens full of fruit trees are still there. These trees grow and make fruit. Food gets very expensive in New Zealand in recent years. People look for ways to get cheap food. They discover the wild gardens full of fruit trees. People pick fruit, nuts, and mushrooms there. Many people look for food. It is cheap. Some people are happy that they spend more time in nature. They see how trees and plants grow. They say that wild fruit tastes much better than fruit from a supermarket. Difficult words: earthquake (when the earth moves, and it destroys houses and other things), dangerous (not safe), discover (to find). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At The Nines in Crans-Montana, Switzerland, Japanese freestyle snowboarder Hiroto Ogiwara landed the world’s first backside 2160. He did six full rotations on his snowboard. The Nines is a biannual freestyle skiing and snowboarding event that alternates between winter and summer events. Some of the world’s top athletes participate in six days of unique action on specially built jumps that produce a spectacular show full of tricks and moves that defy gravity. 16-year-old Ogiwara initially planned to try and land a backside 1800 that he was unable to do the previous day. When he accomplished that quicker than he expected, he decided toward progression . Five attempts later, Ogiwara landed snowboarding’s first-ever backside 2160. Japanese snowboarder Reira Iwabuchi also completed a world first as the first female frontside triple 1260, which is three and a half rotations. Difficult words: alternate (to happen repeatedly), defy (to go against something), progression (development towards an improved situation or state). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

16-year-old Japanese snowboarder Hiroto Ogiwara was the first person who landed a backside 2160. It is when you turn on your snowboard for six full rotations . It happened at The Nines, a freestyle skiing and snowboarding event for the world’s top athletes, which took place in Crans-Montana, Switzerland. The event took six days, and Ogiwara did the trick just before it ended. First, he planned to try a backside 1800. He did well, so he decided to try a backside 2160. Ogiwara’s sixth attempt was successful. Another Japanese snowboarder named Reira Iwabuchi became the first woman to do a frontside triple 1260, or three and a half rotations. Difficult words: rotation (a turn around a center), freestyle (a sport or race without any or with only a few rules), attempt (a try to do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hiroto Ogiwara is a Japanese snowboarder. He is 16 years old. He does something amazing last week. He is the first person in the world who lands a backside 2160. A backside 2160 is a trick with six full rotations while you use your snowboard. It is very difficult. Ogiwara does it at The Nines. The Nines is a freestyle event for the world’s best skiers and snowboarders. It takes place every year. This year, it is in Switzerland. It lasts six days. Ogiwara does the trick on the last day. He doesn’t plan it before the event. Reira Iwabuchi is another Japanese snowboarder. She has a good day, too. She is the first woman in the world who does a frontside triple 1260. A frontside triple 1260 is three and a half rotations. Difficult words: amazing (very great or wonderful), rotation (a turn around), freestyle (a sport or race without any or with only a few rules). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The British singer Ed Sheeran has won a court battle over a plagiarism accusation for his hit single “Shape of You”. “Shape of You” was the world’s best-selling song of 2017 with more than three billion plays on Spotify alone. Sami Chokri, who performs under the name Sami Switch, said the ‘oh I, oh I, oh I’ was strikingly similar to the chorous of his song that he released two years earlier. Sheeran told the court that the contested part of “Shape of You” was very short, and the relevant parts of both songs were common. In a video posted on social media, Sheeran said that he was happy; however, he criticized a growing culture to file baseless claims with the idea that it was cheaper for a songwriter to settle than fight a claim. He said that this practice was damaging to the songwriting industry. Difficult words: plagiarism (to take someone else’s work or ideas and present them as your own), baseless (not based on facts), settle (to stop a fight). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ed Sheeran is a British singer who wrote a song named “Shape of You” in 2017. The song became the best-selling song in the world, and it had more than three billion plays on Spotify. Then another singer named Sami Switch accused Sheeran that he stole a part of his song which he wrote two years earlier. Switch said that the ‘oh I, oh I, oh I’ part was similar to the chorous of his song. Sheeran said that it was usual in pop music that some melodies sound similar. Last week, Sheeran won a court battle against Switch. Sheeran said that he was happy, but he said that it was a hard situation for songwriters . It was cheaper to pay money to the other artist than to fight in court. Difficult words: accuse (to say that someone did something wrong), chorous (a part of a song which repeats more times), songwriter (a person who writes popular songs or the music for them). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ed Sheeran is a British singer. He writes a song named “Shape of You” in 2017. The song becomes one of the most popular songs in the world. Sami Switch is another British singer. He writes a song called “Oh Why”. He writes the song two years before Ed Sheeran writes his song. Switch says that a part of Sheeran’s song is very similar to his own song. Switch says that Sheeran steals a part of the song. The singers go to court . The court decides that Sheeran doesn’t steal the song. Sheeran is happy. He says that it is hard to be a songwriter . People can find thousands of songs. It sometimes happen that some songs sound similar. Difficult words: steal (to take something what belongs to somebody else), court (a group of people who decide if somebody does something wrong and what happens to him), songwriter (a person who writes songs). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The falling prices of Russian crab sent more South Koreans to seafood markets. According to some vendors , the drop in prices doubled the visitors. King crabs from Russia along with smaller snow crabs and lobsters were once a pricey delicacy in South Korea; however, in recent years, they’ve become more popular at supermarkets and online retailers. Since late February, prices have nearly halved as the USA, EU, and others banned Russian seafood imports over the Ukraine invasion. However, for some people, Russian crab isn’t a necessity, and they think that it’s not right to eat it if it’s cheap. They say that the government should join global efforts to ban Russian seafood and customers should refrain from buying it. Difficult words: vendor (a person or company that sells something), delicacy (a rare and expensive food), refrain (to stop yourself from doing something that you want to do). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

As a result of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, many countries in the world banned Russian products. Some countries didn’t, for example, South Korea. Since February, the prices of Russian crab fell. King crab, snow crab, and lobster were very rare and expensive food in the past, but now, people can buy them in supermarkets. Since the start of the war in Ukraine, the number of visitors doubled at seafood markets. Some people don’t care why food from Russia is so cheap, but many people do care. They say that it is not right to eat food from Russia because it is cheap. They say that the government should ban Russian food, and people should stop buying it. Difficult words: ban (to officially stop something), lobster (a large animal which has a hard shell, two large claws, and eight legs), double (to become twice as much or many). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Russia attacks Ukraine in February. Some countries do not buy things from Russia. South Korea still buys things from Russia. Russian things are cheaper. In the past, Russian crabs and lobster are very expensive and rare . Now, people can buy them in supermarkets. The number of visitors of seafood markets doubles . Some people don’t care about the war. They buy Russian seafood. Right now it is cheap. Many people don’t buy it. They say that it is wrong. They say that the government must not buy things from Russia. Difficult words: lobster (a large animal which has a hard shell and eight legs), rare (when there is very little of something), double (to become twice as much or many). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A French store predicts the results of the first round of the presidential election based on the number of sock it sold. The store sells socks depicting the faces of the eight main candidates, and 10 days before the vote, far-right candidate Eric Zemmour was in first place with around 29% of sales. President Emmanuel Macron was at 24%, and Jean-Luc Melenchon was at around 22%. These three faces led, and the other candidates were behind. The company sold thousands of pairs around the world, with Macron socks sold best in Germany, Zemmour socks sold best in Canada, and Melenchon sold best in Greece. However, the vendor said that the main idea was to have fun with everyday products like socks, which could be a unique way to end a campaign. Difficult words: far-right (a political party that is deeply conservative), vendor (a person or company that sells goods or services), unique (unlike anything else). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A French shop sells socks with the faces of the eight main candidates in the presidential election . 10 days before people voted in the first round, the shop predicted the winner. Far-fight candidate Eric Zemmour was first, as socks with his face sold best. 29% of customers bought socks with his face. President Emmanuel Macron was second with 24%, and Jean-Luc Melenchon was third with 22%. The socks sold in many places, as people from all over the world bought them. Socks with the face of President Macron sold best in Germany. People didn’t take the result very seriously. They wanted to have some fun with something basic like socks. Difficult words: presidential election (when people vote who the president will be), far-right (a political party which is very conservative and doesn’t like changes), basic (simple or very usual). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People in France vote for a new president. A shop sells special socks. The faces of eight candidates are on the socks. The shop predicts the president. 29% of customers buy socks with the face of Eric Zemmour. He has strong opinions about immigration and Islam. President Emmanuel Macron is next. 24% of customers buy socks with his face. It is for fun. Nobody really knows who will win. The socks are in many places. People from all around the world buy them. President Macron is the most popular in Germany. Zemmour socks sell best in Canada. Difficult words: candidate (a person who people vote for as a leader), predict (to say what will probably happen in the future), immigration (when people come to live to another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An Indian wife-to-be refused to marry her groom at the altar after he failed a simple maths test of 15 plus 6. The bride’s family claims that they had been misled by the potential suitor from the start, as they had been shown someone else’s photo, as well as lied to about his income and education. The wife-to-be, Lovely, is good at her studies and wants to get married to an educated boy. Both sides of the marriage returned all the received gifts, and local police came to mediate between the families. Difficult words: altar (the place in a church where you get married), potential (possible), suitor (a person who wants to marry another person), mediate (help people in an argument). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A girl in India wants to meet her potential husband for the first time. People show her a photo of him and then she goes to meet him at his home. When she gets there, she is suspicious because he does not look like the boy in the photo. She asks him a math question of 15 plus 6. He answers incorrectly with 17. She refuses to marry him. Her family says that he tricked them, while his family says that she should come back. A friend explains that education is important to the girl. The local police have to mediate for the families. Difficult words: potential (possible), suspicious (thinking someone is doing something wrong), mediate (to help people in an argument). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A girl lives in India. She wants to meet her potential husband. People show her his photo. She goes to meet him. He is not the boy from the photo. She is suspicious . She asks him to do a math problem. It is 15 plus 6. He says the wrong answer. He says 17. She refuses to marry him. Her family says that he tricked them. His family says that she should marry him. A friend says that the girl was a good student. She wants her husband to be a good student. Local police help the families. Difficult words: potential (future), suspicious (when you think something is wrong), refuse (to say no). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

When most people tell you that they have a couple of cats at home, you probably don’t expect them to have lion cubs, but it is true for one family in Gaza. The cubs’ names are Mona and Alex, and they were born in the battle -torn Gaza Strip to parents that were smuggled through a tunnel along the border with Egypt. Gazan refugee Saed Eldin al-Jamal bought the baby lions from a zoo after the economic situation forced the zoo owner to sell them. The owner used to take the cubs back to the zoo every night to be breastfed by their mom, but recently they have been weaned and now live in the family home all the time. The cats also became part of the local community and children play with them when they go out for walks. The cubs look quite at home with the family, but animal experts warned that having lions at home with children can be dangerous and that they will need a more suitable environment when they grow bigger. Difficult words: -torn (destroyed), smuggle (move something from one country to another illegally), refugee (a person who has to leave his or her country), wean (start eating food other than the mother’s milk). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The owner of a zoo in the Gaza Strip had to sell two lion cubs . A 54-year-old man bought them and brought them home – they became his family’s pets. At the beginning, when the cubs were really little, they had to be breastfed by their mum. The man took them to the zoo every night. But the cubs weaned recently, and they live in the family home all of the time. The cats are now part of the local community. Children play with them when they go out for walks. However, experts say that having lions at home with children can be dangerous. The lions will need a better environment when they grow bigger. Difficult words: cub (a young animal), wean (to start eating other food than a mother’s milk), environment (the place where an animal lives). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Gaza. There is a zoo. This zoo does not have enough money. It must sell two lion cubs . A man buys them. He brings them home. The cubs become pets. In the beginning, the cubs need their mother. They must be breastfed . The mother of the cubs lives in the zoo. The man takes them to the zoo every night. Later, the animals grow bigger. They start to eat meat. They don’t need their mother anymore. People like the little lions. Children play with them. However, the cubs will get big. They will be dangerous. Difficult words: cub (a young animal), breastfeed (when a mother gives her baby milk), will (this means “in the future”). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

For more than 20 years, researchers from Columbia University have ran a long-term study on autism. The study involved more than 115,000 children, and it investigated the causes of autism and possible ways to prevent it. According to scientists, strong genetic factors were part of it. The study involved blood and genetic testing and detailed health questionnaires. It found three different factors caused autism which were certain genes, the environmental conditions, and the time of these events. Multiple circumstances created the conditions for autism. They were specifically inflammation in the body and a high fever during the second trimester of the pregnancy, when critical neural pathways develop in the unborn baby. The study showed that some children were at a lower risk of having autism if their mothers took ibuprofen to treat the fever. It’s estimated that one in 44 children in the US has been diagnosed with autism. Difficult words: trimester (a period of three months), neural pathway (the nerves or the nervous system), ibuprofen (a drug that treats fever and pain). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

For 20 years, scientists at an American university studied autism. The study involved more than 115,000 children, and scientists wanted to learn the causes of autism and ways to prevent it. Scientists took blood samples, they did genetic tests, and all people in the study answered many questions about their health. The study found that three important things impacted autism. They were genetics, health, and the time that events happened. The study also showed that the second trimester of the pregnancy was very important, as the child’s brain developed in this time. When a pregnant woman had a high fever in the second trimester, and she didn’t treat the fever, it could cause autism. Reports say that one in 44 children in the US has autism. Difficult words: prevent (to stop something from happening), genetic (information in the body) trimester (three months). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Autism is a disorder . A person with autism has problems when he wants to talk and interact with others. Studies say that one in 44 children in the US have autism. Scientists from university study autism for 20 years. They work with 115,000 children. They check the children’s blood and genetic markers . Scientists also need a lot of information about the children’s health. The study shows that there are three important things, which can cause autism. The first thing is specific genetic markers. The second thing is health. The last thing is the timing of these two things. Pregnant women must be careful. The child’s brain develops in the second trimester . When a pregnant woman has a high fever in this time, it can cause autism. It is important to take pills, which stop the fever. Difficult words: disorder (when something doesn’t work the usual way), genetic marker (specific information in the body), trimester (three months). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hungary’s nationalist prime minister Viktor Orbán declared victory in the national election, winning a fourth consecutive term. In his speech, Orbán responded to criticism from the Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskiy. Zelenskiy repeatedly challenged Orbán over his lack of support to Ukraine and unwillingness to condemn his ally Vladimir Putin for the invasion in Ukraine. Orbán also refused to allow weapons to Ukraine or military aid to pass through Hungarian territory. Orbán’s party has strengthened its hold on the government through supporting media that supports them and through changes to the voting system. Critics said the changes made elections unfair. The ruling party has retained its two-thirds majority, so it has changed Hungarian politics and social policies. Difficult words: nationalist (a person who strongly supports political independence), condemn (to criticize something or someone strongly, usually for moral reasons), retain (to keep or continue to have something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hungary’s prime minister Viktor Orbán won in the national election for the fourth time consecutively , and for the fifth time altogether. Orbán’s nationalist party was even stronger thanks to his power on the media. Also, he changed the voting system, and some people said that it made the voting unfair. His party won two-thirds of the seats in the government, which gave him a lot of power to change Hungarian politics. Some people criticized Orbán, as he supported the Russian president Vladimir Putin. Orbán met Putin twelve times in the past, and he said that Hungary needed Russian oil and gas. Orbán gave Ukraine no weapons to fight against Russia, and he also stopped other countries’ weapons to go through Hungary. Difficult words: election (to vote a person for a job in politics), consecutive (in a row), nationalist (with strong belief that a country is independent). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Viktor Orbán is the Hungarian prime minister. He wins the elections again last weekend. Orbán is prime minister four times before. This is the fifth time. Some people are not happy. Orbán owns some media . He can tell journalists what to write. Orbán’s party changes how people vote. Many people believe that it is not fair. Orbán’s party has most of the power in parliament. Orbán meets with the Russian president Vladimir Putin many times. Orbán says that Hungary needs oil and gas from Russia. Hungary doesn’t give Ukraine any weapons to fight against Russia. Other countries can’t give weapons to Ukraine through Hungary. Difficult words: elections (an event when people choose a person for a job in politics), media (the TV, radio, and newspapers), party (a government group). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Afghan farmers collected their first opium harvest of the season in the southern province of Helmand, despite Taliban’s ban on narcotics farming. Taliban also strictly banned the export and production of any intoxicants , such as wine, heroin, or cannabis. Each year, workers from all around the country gather in Helmand for the harvest season. First, they make small cuts on the poppy pods in the afternoon, and the next morning, they collect the opium, that comes out of the pods. Each worker is paid six dollars per day during the 15-days harvest season. One kilogram of opium is sold for 68 to 114 dollars, depending on the quality. According to reports, Afghanistan continues to be the world’s largest producer of opium, and the production of the narcotic contributed up to 11% to the country’s economy. Difficult words: opium (a bitter brownish drug that comes from the juice of the opium poppy), narcotic (an illegal drug such as heroin or cocaine), intoxicant (a substance that makes feelings of pleasure or happiness). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

This year, Taliban made a stricter law about drugs not to grow the poppy for opium. Taliban also stopped trade and selling of wine, heroin, cannabis and other drugs. Farmers in the Afghan province of Helmand ignored the law, and last week, they harvested opium. Helmand is a place where many farmers come every year to harvest opium. First, they make small cuts on part of the poppy that is a pod. The next day, they collect the juice, which comes from the pod. Opium is a very powerful drug from the dried juice. Farmers harvest opium for 15 days, and they get six dollars for one day of work. Afghanistan makes the most opium in the world, and the opium makes 11% of the country’s business. Difficult words: poppy (a plant with large red flowers and small black seeds), ignore (to not notice something on purpose), harvest (to collect). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Taliban makes a new law about drugs. The law says that Afghanistan farmers must not grow poppy for opium. The poppy is a plant with large red flowers. It has a pod which is full of black seeds. Farmers cut the pod. The next day, they get the juice which comes out from the pod. People then dry the juice. They make opium from the dry juice. Opium is a very strong drug. It has a yellowish-brown color. It smells strongly. It is an illegal drug. Farmers harvest opium for the first time this year. The Afghan area of Helmand is a popular place to grow poppy. Farmers from all the country come here. Opium makes a lot of the country’s money. Difficult words: pod (a case, in which are seeds of some plants), illegal (against the rules of a country), harvest (to pick fruit or crops when it is time to eat it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

For countries that neighbor Russia, the war in Ukraine feels very close, and they wonder if they’re next. In the past, the Soviet Union was an equal to the US as a global superpower. At its height, it dominated Eastern Europe, and it encompassed 15 republics. The Soviet Union fell in 1991, and Russian president Vladimir Putin then called it a catastrophe. Since that time, Russia tried to reoccupy some of its previous territories, for example, Crimea and Ukraine. Among the most concerned are the small Baltic countries of Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia. They are squeezed between Russia and Belarus, and they have a long and painful history of Russian occupation. Unlike Ukraine, the three Baltic nations have been part of the EU and NATO. If Russia ever invades them, the US and other allies will come to defend them. Difficult words: dominate (to have power and influence over someone or something), encompass (to include), ally (a group that formally cooperates with another for a military or other purpose). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In the past, Russia was in the Soviet Union, which was a superpower just like the US. At one time, the Soviet Union had 15 republics, including Ukraine and Belarus. The Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, but Russia tried to get some parts of it again. Now, Russia is trying to get Ukraine again. Some countries worry that are close to Russia; they worry that Russia could attack them in the future, too. For example, they are the Baltic countries. The Baltic countries are three small countries between Russia and Belarus. They are Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia. Some people already contacted their families and friends in other countries, as they worry that Russia will attack them. If it happens, the US and other countries will help them because they are part of the EU and NATO, and NATO members defend each other. Difficult words: superpower (a country which has a lot of power), collapse (to fall), defend (to keep safe from an attack). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Baltic countries are three small countries between Russia and Belarus. They are Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia. These countries are a part of the Soviet Union in the past. The Soviet Union has a lot of power in the 20 th century. 15 countries belong to the Soviet Union. For example, they are Russia, Ukraine and Belarus. The Soviet Union falls apart in 1991. Later, Russia wants some countries again. For example, Russia occupies Crimea in 2014. Now Russia attacks Ukraine. The Baltic countries worry that Russia will attack them, too. It is a different situation. They belong to the EU and NATO. Other NATO members will help them. Difficult words: fall apart (to break into small things), occupy (to control something), member (a person or thing which is a part of a group of more similar persons or things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The cost of growing cucumber climbs in the UK due to soaring energy prices. For three generations, Tony Montalbano’s family has farmed cucumbers in the southeast of England, and he’s supplied major supermarkets. However, 30,000 square meters of the company’s greenhouses are empty. They would normally be full of fully grown plants. The rising cost of energy has stopped the company from using heat to grow the plants. Montalbano decided not to plant the first of the year’s three cycles in January, hoping that gas prices would drop. However, that didn’t happen, and gas costs much more than last year. Last year, it cost about 25 pence to grow a cucumber in the UK. The price has doubled, and it could cost 70 pence when energy prices rise. The cost of fertilizer and labor has also soared, and farmers have not planted peppers, tomatoes, and other plants. Difficult words: soar (to increase very quickly), cycle (events or actions that repeat regularly), fertilizer (a substance that farmers add to soil to make plants grow better). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

It means that it’s too cold for the plants to grow. Last year, it cost 25 pence to grow one cucumber. Now, the price almost doubled, and experts say that it could soon be as high as 70 pence. Also, the prices of fertilizer and employees are growing, too. Other farmers who grow plants like peppers and tomatoes are having the same problems. Difficult words: supply (to give a large amount of something to people or companies who want to buy it), greenhouse (a special building where people grow plants), fertilizer (a substance which farmers put in the soil to make plants grow better). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

According to his family, American actor Bruce Willis is retiring from acting after being diagnosed with a disease that was impacting his cognitive abilities. The disease is aphasia. Aphasia is a condition that affects a person’s ability to communicate. It can affect the speech and comprehension of both spoken and written language. Typically, aphasia occurs suddenly after a stroke or a head injury. If a person works in a profession that requires language and he has aphasia, he will have difficulties. Willis, who’s 67, achieved initial fame for the 1980s TV series ‘Moonlighting’ before he became an action hero in five ‘Die Hard’ films. The actor has appeared in about 100 films, and he won acclaim for his roles in ‘Pulp Fiction’ and ‘The Sixth Sense’. Difficult words: cognitive (related to thinking, learning, and understanding things), stroke (a sudden attack in the body which occurs the brain doesn’t get enough blood), acclaim (strong approval or praise). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Wednesday, the family of American actor Bruce Willis announced that he suffers from aphasia. Aphasia is a disease which impacts a person’s ability to speak and to understand what other people speak or write. The disease usually starts after a stroke or a head injury. If a person has aphasia and he works in a job with language, it can cause a big impact on his work. For that reason, Willis decided to retire . The 67-year-old actor became famous in the 1980s thanks to the TV series ‘Moonlighting’. He then played in five ‘Die Hard’ films, which made him an international star. He played in more than 100 films, and eight of them were in 2021. They weren’t Willis’s best films, but fans still loved the actor, and the news about his disease shocked them. Difficult words: ability (the skill or power to do something), stroke (a sudden attack when the brain doesn’t get enough blood), retire (to stop working). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

He plays in the TV series ‘Moonlighting’. He plays in five ‘Die Hard’ films. He becomes very popular in all the world. His fans love him. The news about Willis’s disease is a shock for them. Difficult words: disease (a situation when a part of the body doesn’t work as usual, and the person becomes ill), retire (to stop working, usually after working many years), shock (bad or surprising news or event which somebody doesn’t expect). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

China’s most populous city tightened the first stage of a two-stage lockdown, and officials asked residents to stay indoors. China’s financial hub is in one of its longest lockdowns, and two years since the start of the pandemic, streets are empty again. The 25-million city closed bridges and tunnels which split the city in two along the Huangpu River. Residents living on the river’s eastern bank had to stay at home for four days, and on the western bank, lockdown started four days later. Officials earlier attempted to keep the city running by limiting lockdowns to certain neighborhoods or buildings; however, the city struggled to control new cases. Some residents were surprised by the restrictions, and they woke up to find a fence around their compounds . The lockdown came at the time when the city was battling a surge in Omicron cases, which had been challenging China’s zero-COVID strategy. Difficult words: hub (the center of an activity), compound (a group of buildings), surge (a sudden increase). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Shanghai, China’s biggest city, went into lockdown again. The lockdown split the city into two different parts. On the eastern bank of the Huangpu River, people went into lockdown on Monday. Officials asked them to stay indoors, but some people didn’t know about it. When they woke up that morning, there were fences in the streets. On the western bank of the river, people started the lockdown four days later. Some people agreed with the lockdown, and they said that it was necessary to control the virus. Others were very angry, and they said that they felt like they were in prison. The cases of COVID started to increase again, and China tried hard to stop the coronavirus from spreading. Difficult words: bank (the land along a river), fence (a barrier, usually around someone’s house or a piece of land), necessary (something so important that a person must do it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: lockdown (a situation when people cannot move freely, and they must stay in their homes), bank (the land along a river), fence (a barrier around someone’s house or a piece of land). One farmer from Kansas, USA decided to create cow art. He used his cattle, a feed truck and drones to create a huge smiley face out of cows. If that is not enough to make you smile, the farmer and artist is also known for using his trombone to herd the cows, saying that they have happy cows in Kansas. Difficult words: huge (very big), trombone (a musical instrument like a horn). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

NASA released a captivating time-lapse video showing some of the most memorable moments of the sun’s activity in the last 5 years. To make the footage, someone captured one frame of the sun every eight hours from June 2010 to February 8 th , 2015. Then NASA released the footage in honour of the Solar Dynamics Observatory’s fifth anniversary. The observatory’s aims are to improve our understanding of the sun’s energy and its effects on Earth and near-Earth space. Highlights of the footage include clouds of solar material being thrown into space and loops hovering in the atmosphere, which is known as the corona . Different colours in the video represent different wavelengths of extreme ultraviolet light , ultraviolet light and visible light which in turn correspond to solar material at different temperatures. Difficult words: hover (remain in one place in space), captivating (very interesting), corona (the circle of light around the sun), ultraviolet light (a type of light that is very strong but we cannot see it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

NASA’s scientists took a picture of the sun every eight hours from June 2010 to February 2015. They put the pictures together and created a time-lapse video. Make sure to check it out! You can see how the sun hurls solar material into space. This material which stays around the sun is known as the corona . The scientists also studied the sun’s energy and its effects on earth. Difficult words: hurl (to throw), solar (relating to the sun), corona (the circle of light around the sun). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: create (to make), affect (to change), Earth (“our” planet). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last week on Monday, heavy fighting started in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Fighters from the M23 rebel group attacked the army near the border with Uganda and Rwanda. The fighting began approximately 50 kilometers northeast of the provincial capital of Goma. Troops came to respond and chase the enemy; however, it wasn’t clear who was in control of the area. In November 2021, the M23 briefly seized the two strategic villages in a similar overnight attack. The villages were the last strongholds of the M23 before soldiers chased its fighters into Uganda and Rwanda in 2013. Since then, there have been efforts to establish dialogue and disarmament ; however, they haven’t been successful. Difficult words: seize (to take something by force), stronghold (a well defended place), disarmament (when you take away or give up weapons). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: rebel (a person who fights against the government), strategic (very important), chase (to run after someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Actor Will Smith smacked Chris Rock at the Oscars 2022 after Rock made a joke about Smith’s wife’s hair. Rock joked to Smith that he was looking forward to a sequel to ‘G. I. Jane’. Smith stood up, walked up to Rock, and he slapped him. After returning to his seat, Smith cursed at Rock. Shortly after the confrontation , Will Smith won the Oscar for the best actor for ‘King Richard’. In 2018, Jada Pinkett Smith revealed that she’d been diagnosed with alopecia, hair loss that can affect the scalp or the entire body. It often results in a few bald spots on the scalp, and it can be temporary or permanent. Stress and illness are the possible causes; however in most cases, there’s no obvious trigger . Difficult words: curse (to use offensive words in anger or annoyance), confrontation (a face-to-face meeting between two people, who are angry, or they disagree with each other), trigger (to cause a reaction). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Actor Will Smith smacked Oscar host Chris Rock at the Oscars 2022. Rock made a joke about Smith’s wife Jada Pinkett Smith. Rock said that he was looking forward to ‘G. I. Jane 2’. G. I. Jane was a movie from 1997 with Demi Moore, who had a very short haircut. The joke meant that Smith looked similar to G. I. Jane. Alopecia is a disease when a person loses hair. The patient often has spots with no hair on the scalp , but sometimes it can affect the whole body. Scientists don’t know what causes this disease, but they think that stress and illness can cause it. Difficult words: smack (to hit someone with the hand), spot (a specific place or point), scalp (the skin on the head). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
